intended_object: The line (directional) derivative of f at x in direction v within a set s: the derivative at t = 0 of t ↦ f(x + t•v), restricted to the parameters t with x + t•v ∈ s, and 0 if it does not exist. Inferred from the docstring and the name.
explanation: The body is `derivWithin (fun t ↦ f (x + t • v)) ((fun t ↦ x + t • v) ⁻¹' s) 0`. This is exactly the one-variable derivative within the preimage of s along the line through x in direction v, which is the standard definition of the directional derivative within a set. The junk value 0 matches the docstring. The generality is maximal: E only needs to be a 𝕜-module, since no topology on E is used, and F is a normed space over any nontrivially normed field. This declaration is itself in Mathlib, and there is no other, more general Mathlib definition of the same notion (fderivWithin applied to v is a different, stronger notion).
